chunks: From him, from Ahmad, from Dawood ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn al-Fayz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Ja'far, meaning Abu al-Dawaniq, when a packet came to him. He untied it and looked inside, then took something out from it. He said, 'O Abu Abdillah, do you know what this is?' I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'This is something that comes from behind Africa, from Tangier or Tubna (Muhammad doubted). I said, 'What is it?' He said, 'There is a mountain there from which drops drip in a year and solidify. It is good for the whiteness that occurs in the eye; if this is applied to it, it will go away by the permission of Allah, Mighty and Majestic.'

I said, 'Yes, I know it, and if you wish, I will inform you of its name and its condition.' He said, 'He did not ask me about its name.' He said, 'And what is its condition?' So I said, 'This is a mountain on which a Prophet from the Prophets of the Children of Israel was hiding from his people, worshipping Allah upon it. So his people learned about it and killed him. So it (the mountain) weeps over that Prophet (peace be upon him), and these drops are from his weeping. And on the other side of it is a spring from which that water flows by night and by day, and it does not reach that fountain (of tears).'

key_terms.خَرِيطَةٌ: A packet or bundle wrapped in cloth
key_terms.طَنْجَةَ: Tangier, a city in North Africa
key_terms.طُبْنَةَ: Tabna, a place in North Africa
key_terms.يُكْتَحَلُ: To apply kohl or medicine to the eye

ai.seo_question: What is the origin and medicinal use of the drops from the weeping mountain in Africa?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies a medicinal resin from Ifriqiya as the tears of a mountain mourning a Prophet of the Children of Israel, illustrating the Shia concept of *al-Bukra* (the morning/early time) where creation reflects spiritual realities. This account highlights the intersection of natural medicine (*tibb*) and metaphysical history, emphasizing that physical remedies often carry the imprint of divine events and prophetic sacrifices.

en.hubeali: H 15029 – From him, from Ahmad, from Dawood Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Al-Fayz, who has narrated the following: Abu Abdullahasws has said: ‘

I<sup>asws</sup> was in the presence of Abu Ja’far, meaning Abu Al-Dawaniq, when a packet came and he opened it and looked inside it. So he took something out from it. He said, ‘O Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, do you<sup>asws</sup> know what this is?’ I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is it?’ He said, ‘This is something that has come to me from behind Africa, from Tanjat, (or Tabnat, Muhammad (the narrator doubted). So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘What is it?’ He said, ‘There is a mountain there from which drops come out in a year and solidify, and it is best for the whiteness which occurs in the eyes, if this is applied to them, it would go away by the Permission of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic.

I<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘Yes, I recognise it, and if you like I can inform you of its name and its condition’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He never asked me<sup>asws</sup> about its name’. He said, ‘And what is its condition?’ So I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is a mountain on which was a Prophet<sup>as</sup> from the sons of the Children of Israel, who had fled from his<sup>as</sup> people, and he<sup>as</sup> used to worship upon it. So the people came to know about it, and they killed him. So it (mountain) now weeps over that Prophet<sup>as</sup>, and these are the drops from its weeping. And on the other side of it is a spring from which the water flows by the night and the day, but it does not arrive to that fountain (of tears)’.
en.sarwar: 583. Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Suleym the slave of Ali Bin Yaqteen, who has said: He said: ‘I had conjunctivitis in my eye which hurt. ‘Abu Al-Hassan (a.s.) wrote to me about it initiating from himself (a.s.); ‘What is preventing you from applying the application of Abu Ja’far (a.s.), a part of Rabahiyya Camphor, Aloe of Asqutry, crushed together and sifted by silk. You should apply from it like the application from the powder, once in a month.
It would chase away every illness in the head and exit it from the body’. He said, ‘He used to apply it, and had no complaints for his eyes until death’.
